This application sets a process for acceptance including inspections and the submission of required supporting documents and inspections. . 
As Built Plans must be submitted as part of this process. Please read and follow the City's standards for as-built drawings which can be found in the Hilliard Engineering Design Manual (https://hilliard.municipalcodeonline.com/book?type=designs#name=1.7_As_Built_Plans_And_Final_Utility_Data_Submission). A one year warranty period after acceptance is required.

record_types.name: Solicitor & Peddler Permit
record_types.text:
An individual needs a solicitation permit if they do any of the following: obtain or seek to obtain funds or donations for commercial purposes; knock on doors, ring doorbells or talk to residents as they go door to door; peddles goods of any nature for immediate or future sale; or obtains orders or sets appointments for a future service or sale. 
Detailed requirements and regulations governing solicitation within the City of Hilliard can be found in Chapter 745 of the City of Hilliard's Codified Ordinances (https://library.municode.com/oh/hilliard/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=PTSEVENBURECO_CH745CAPESO). 
In order to complete this permit application you will need to obtain your BCI Webcheck background results. You can find a listing of Webcheck locations here: Webcheck Community Listing - Ohio Attorney General Dave Yost (https://www.ohioattorneygeneral.gov/business/services-for-business/webcheck/webcheck-community-listing)
Note: Canvassers, defined as "Any person who seeks to disseminate any verbal or written lawful message including ideas, thoughts or messages regarding any cause, issue or religion without soliciting funds or donations; or any political candidate without acting as a solicitor and whose actions do not violate any local, state or federal law" are not required to register with the City of Hilliard. 
Persons who are under 18 who are not employed by another person or company do not need to apply for a permit.

record_types.summary: Review for commercial improvements, and new buildings, residential additions that do not meet the planning and zoning code requirements, conditional use, home occupation. This includes all Variance Requests that are not related to signage.
record_types.text:
NOTE: A description of each Board of Zoning Appeals application is provided below. If you are still unsure of the application your project requires, please contact the Planning Division at:
Email: jtalentino@hilliardohio.gov (mailto:jtalentino@hilliardohio.gov)
Phone: 614-334-2444
Application Types and Associated Fees: 
• Administrative Appeal: an application to appeal an administrative decision issued by a city code enforcement officer. • Any property within Hilliard ($300.00)
• Temporary Land Use: an application to temporarily dedicate structures or premises for uses not wholly consistent with the approved uses of the zoning district in which the parcel is located. Fees vary depending on location of parcel:• Any property within Hilliard ($300.00)
• Nonconformities: an application to extend a nonconforming use, change an existing nonconforming use to another nonconforming use, or extend or enlarge a nonconforming structure ($200).
• Variance: an application to deviate from one or more dimensional provisions or requirements of the city’s Planning and Zoning Code (https://library.municode.com/oh/hilliard/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=PTELEVENPLZOCO), including by way of example, lot size, width, setbacks, parking requirements and height, applicable to the applicant's property. Fees vary depending on location and use of parcel:• Any property within the Old Hilliard District ($300)
• A single-family development not in the Old Hilliard District ($300)
• All others ($1,000)
• Other: an application regarding matters that may otherwise be provided by the City's Codified Ordinances or other codes adopted by the City ($200).
Information Required for Submission:
• Name, contact information, and address of applicant;
• Address, parcel/tax ID number, and Zoning District of property in question;
• Description of project;
• Name, contact information, and address of attorney/agent (if applicable);
• A digital copy of the site plan that shows existing conditions (street right of way, easements, property lines, etc.) and proposed changes (elevations, site plans, landscaping plans, and lighting plans); and
• A digital list of the names and addresses of all property owners within 200 feet of property in question.

record_types.name: Commercial Plan Review
record_types.summary:
Plans for commercial projects must be submitted for review before obtaining construction permits .    A. 2 step process. 1.Commercial Plan Review (PLR). 2. Building Permit-Commercial (CBLD).
Plans may be submitted by owners, designers, contractors or other agents of the owner, however, plan review results/comments will only be shared with the applicant or guest email addresses added to the record.    
Plan Reviews may take up to to 30 days to complete.  Plans are reviewed in the order they are submitted with no projects expedited ahead of other projects.
record_types.text:
Commercial Plan Review 
Once you begin the application, you will be able to upload plans or documents. Corrections, changes or additional information to a submittal can be uploaded as additional attachments to the existing record. Keep in mind that you can return to any application at any time and send comments to City staff or complete any other step in the workflow. To access any of your records after you log in, select “My Account” from the home screen.
**REVISED PLANS SHALL INCLUDE A BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE CHANGES AND ANY CHANGES TO THE PLANS SHALL BE HIGHLIGHTED OR CLOUDED. 
During the application process, you will be asked to upload documents. You must submit the following:
1. Submit Electronic Plans and Construction Documents for Plan Review. Please combine individual pdfs into one document for easier viewing. Note: there is a 100 MB limit per file however, you can upload multiple files. All files must be in an unlocked pdf format. 
2. For New Buildings or Additions: Submit a Statement of Special Inspections. Pursuant to section 1704.3 Ohio Building Code, this statement of special inspections must be prepared by the registered design professional in responsible charge acting as the owner’s agent. This statement (2-part documents) should be submitted as a condition for plan approval and should include the following: 
 • Part I: A complete list of materials and work requiring special inspections and the required frequency of inspections by sections 1705.1 through 1705.18 Ohio Building Code. 
 • Part II: A list of special inspectors who are qualified and are competent to the particular type of construction or operations. These special inspectors shall be employed by the owner or by the registered design professional in responsible charge acting as the owner’s agent. Submit proper resumes and/or certificates of the special inspectors. 
3. Any additional documentation such as energy code requirements and specifications can also be submitted at this time.
4. Plumbing drawings are reviewed by Franklin County Public Health. Here is the link to their website: https://myfcph.org/environmental-health/plumbing/ (https://myfcph.org/environmental-health/plumbing/). The contact person is Sandy at: 614.525.3635. The approval document from Franklin County must be submitted with the application for a Plumbing Permit.
Note: Once downloaded plans are stamped approved, the applicant is required to print a full size set of these approved plans and the Plan Approval certificate to be kept at the job site for reference by the inspectors (plans can be printed from this site.)
Adopted State of Ohio Building Codes:
The 2017 Ohio Building Code (OBC) is based on the 2015 International Building Code (IBC). 
Hard and electronic versions are available from ICC (www.iccsafe.org) and Thompson-Reuters.
Link to State of Ohio e-codes: Ohio Building Code (http://www.com.ohio.gov/documents/AG%2093%20OBC%20Adoption%20Announcement.pdf)
COMMERCIAL PLAN REVIEW FEES
$100.00 MINIMUM
0-4000 sf. (round up to next 100 sf.) $0.20/sf.
4001-10000 sf. (round up to next 100 sf.) $0.15/sf.
10001-25000 sf. (round up to next 100 sf.) $0.10/sf.

record_types.name: Developer Reimbursement Request
record_types.summary: Used to initiate reimbursement requests for public infrastructure that was constructed as part of a private development or construction project.
record_types.text:
This form should be used by persons who are seeking reimbursement for the construction of public infrastructure under the terms of an approved Development Agreement. 
Prior to submission, the public infrastructure eligible for reimbursement must have been formally accepted by Hilliard City Council (https://hilliardoh.portal.opengov.com/categories/1084/record-types/6551). 
As part of submission, you will be required to provide:
• A copy of the signed Development Agreement. It is important that your reimbursement request aligns with the list of reimbursable expenses included within the Development Agreement. 
• A completed Affidavit of Compliance for Prevailing Wages (https://com.ohio.gov/wps/wcm/connect/gov/749c507f-8148-49aa-9708-932517aec1fe/dico+Affidavit+Of+Contractor+Compliance.pdf?MOD=AJPERES&CONVERT_TO=url&CACHEID=ROOTWORKSPACE.Z18_K9I401S01H7F40QBNJU3SO1F56-749c507f-8148-49aa-9708-932517aec1fe-nVLiKUH)available from the Ohio Bureau of Wage and Hour. 
• Substantiate Eligible Costs. Developer shall provide documentation for all eligible infrastructure costs. This shall include:• A copy of Construction-Related Costs in the form of a final pay request from the contractor including all final quantities, change orders, and release of any retainage. The specific items and quantities that are eligible for reimbursement should be clearly identified. 
• If Design-Related Costs are part of reimbursement request, Developer shall include copies of all Engineer invoices with costs for eligible infrastructure highlighted. 
• A summary sheet of eligible construction and design related costs shall be included as part of your submission.

record_types.text:
Plan Review Fee Spreadsheet (https://hilliardohio-my.sharepoint.com/:x:/g/personal/jcox_hilliardohio_gov/Efia2o3k-BtKvcVWhumxCHgB13ovVyLdgBlv_uW3NdVK0Q?e=OBGnMY)
Construction Inspection Fee Spreadsheet (https://hilliardohio-my.sharepoint.com/:x:/g/personal/jcox_hilliardohio_gov/EauI8ahEDqFKqSWZkvWwkJcBjxtom1a24saYF6NBmLlQ_Q?e=cs9DHF)
Private Development Plan Review and Construction Inspection Fee Guide (https://hilliardohio-my.sharepoint.com/:x:/g/personal/jcox_hilliardohio_gov/EaFpE3PfzJBHrXFGhc7D_AEBFsDv1Rr94leY7LYOByfVOg?e=sCPeaz)
A completed spreadsheet detailing unit costs needs to be uploaded as an attachment to the Civil/Site Plan Review application on a subsequent page. 
A complete copy of the Plan Review and Inspection Fee Policy (https://hilliard.municipalcodeonline.com/book?type=designs#name=1.3_Engineering_Plan_Review_And_Construction_Inspection_Fees) can be viewed here. 
Street Names: Note that project submissions involving new public or private streets must utilize proposed street names on the initial set of civil plans that is submitted. You will also be asked to submit alternative street names as a separate attachment in case there is a naming conflict with one of the street names that is being proposed.
Addressing: Final addressing for new residential units or commercial spaces will occur concurrently with the issuance of building permits. However, utility and construction addresses that are needed prior to, or with, the start of construction can be issued with the review of civil plans. You will be asked to upload a map depicting the location of needed construction or utility addresses with the submission of civil plans. 
Use of Standard Construction Costs:
An Ohio registered professional engineer shall prepare an estimate of the construction cost based on unit prices. This estimate shall be submitted to the City Engineer for review and approval. Once approved this engineer’s estimate shall be used to determine the amount of plan review and inspection fees that are to be paid by the developer and/or applicant.
Rate of Fees:
Fees for plan review for subdivisions shall be four (4) percent of the estimated construction costs for all public improvements or modifications, as described above. 
Fees for private improvements such as commercial/industrial site plans shall be four (4) percent of the estimated construction costs for the public improvements associated with the development plush storm water management and erosion and sediment control provisions, site grading, sidewalks, driveways etc. that fall under public purview. 
In addition to the review fees for the public improvements portions of private civil site plans a plan review fee shall be two (2) percent of the estimated cost of the private work that is subject to the purview of the City Engineer for code compliance and engineering standards.
Fees for inspection services shall be ten (10) percent of the estimated construction costs for all public improvements or modifications, as described above.
Plan Review Fee Reconciliation
A final certified cost estimate shall be submitted on the "Final Project Cost Estimate" form, based upon the final approved plan quantities shown on the construction drawings fully approved by the appropriate review agencies. The amount of the previously submitted fees shall be subtracted from the final estimated total cost to determine the balance of plan review fees due.

record_types.summary: Application to operate any establishment that falls under the designation of a massage or bath establishment as defined by city code. Please click “Select” for full description of qualifying establishments.
record_types.text:
Massage Code:
"Bath Establishment" means any establishment having a fixed place of business where any person, firm, association or corporation engages in, or carries on, or permits to be engaged in or carried on any activity involving any type of physical contact between a patron and an employee or operator, as defined in this section, when that contact is related to providing any form of sauna, shower, steam bath, electric light bath, shower bath, tub bath, hot tub bath, sponge bath, sun bath, mineral bath, Finnish, Swedish or Turkish bath, giving salt glows, or administration of fomentation
"Massage" means any method of pressure on or friction against or stroking, kneading, rubbing, tapping, pounding, vibrating, moving, touching or stimulating the soft tissues of the body with the hands or with the aid of any mechanical or electrical apparatus or appliance, with or without such supplementary aids as rubbing alcohol, liniment, antiseptics, oils, powders, creams, lotion, ointments or other similar preparations commonly used in this practice as defined in Ohio Revised Code Chapter 4731.15.
"Massage Establishment" means any establishment having a fixed place of business where any person, firm, association or corporation engages in, or carries on, or permits to be engaged in or carried on any of the activities of Massage Services, as defined in this section, for any consideration whatsoever and as defined in Ohio Revised Code 503.40.
"Mobile Massage Services" means services in which a licensed massage therapist gives, performs, or administers to another person Massage Services, as defined in this section, for compensation or consideration at a location other than a registered Massage or Bath Establishment. 
Fees:
• Application fee $150
• Notification of new employee fee ($50 for each new employee)

NOTE: A description of each Planning and Zoning Commission application is provided below. If you are still unsure of the application your project requires, please contact the Planning Division at:
Email: jtalentino@hilliardohio.gov (mailto:jtalentino@hilliardohio.gov)
Phone: 614-334-2444
Application Types and Associated Fees:
• Old Hilliard District Plan: an application for any developments, additions, or change of exterior colors and/or building materials occurring within the Old Hilliard District, as defined by the city’s zoning map ($300.00). 
• Limited Overlay: an application to modify the exertion of the provisions of a zoning district to a particular parcel by limiting permitted uses, increasing one or more of the minimum development standards, and/or adding conditions for items not covered by the minimum standards ($850).
• Rezoning: an application to change the zoning designation of a particular parcel to a different zoning designation. Fees vary depending on proposed zoning of parcel:• Any single-family residential property less than 5 acres ($1,100)
• All other zoning districts ($3,100)
• PUD Final Development Plan: an application for the approval of the plans of a Planned Unit Development; approval may be granted for individual phases if the development is to be constructed in two or more phases ($1,000). 
• Modification of PUD Zoning/Final Development Plan: an application to alter the conditions of a previously approved Planned Unit Development. Fees vary depending on current zoning of parcel:• Residential ($350)
• Commercial ($600)

record_types.name: Sanitary Backflow Device Program Application
record_types.text:
OVERVIEW
A sanitary sewer backup occurs when water enters your home through the basement floor drain which is connected to the sanitary sewer system. Backups can occur for multiple reasons, one common cause is an obstruction caused by tree roots or items that shouldn’t be flushed entering the pipe connecting your home to the main sewer. Others can be obstructions in the main sewer line or a system overload during periods of heavy rain. 
For those residents who experience a sanitary sewer backup during a rain event, the City has created a program to assist in identifying the cause of the issue and add measures to help prevent a future sanitary sewer backup. Thru the installation of a sanitary backflow preventer installed on the sewer lateral, a resident can minimize the chance for sewage to enter a basement during a rain event. However, when in operation, the devices also limit the household capacity to discharge sewage. 
 | | 
BASEMENT FLOODING PREVENTION – UNDERSTANDING THE SOURCE
In Hilliard, the sanitary and storm systems are designed to operate separately – with sewage from residences & businesses discharging into the sanitary sewer system and rainwater & storm runoff discharging into the storm water system. Even though the systems are separate, rainwater can enter the sanitary sewer through cracks, root intrusion, and pipe joints; there may also be instances of inappropriate private installations, connecting sump pumps, downspouts, or other storm drains to the sanitary sewer.
When storm water has the ability to enter the sanitary pipes, this can cause the sanitary system to be overwhelmed during periods of intense rainfall. If you experience water entering your basement through the flood drain during a heavy rain event, it is likely due to storm water intrusion in the sanitary system. If the water is entering your home through the walls or foundation, this is more likely to be a sump pump failure or a problem with your downspout lines.
PROGRAM ELIGIBILITY & APPLICATION PROCESS
To assist in situations where homeowners have experienced repeated basement flooding events due to sanitary sewer backups due to rain events, the City has created a sanitary sewer backflow preventer program. This program will help fund the cost of installing a backflow preventer in the basement floor, or on the sanitary lateral, that is designed to prevent sewage from entering a basement thru a floor drain. 
To participate in the City’s Backflow Prevention Program, homeowners will need to fill our this form detailing the nature of the flooding along with some details about your property, and have your property inspected to ensure that it meets the program eligibility requirements.

When is a Certificate of Zoning Compliance (CZC) needed?
An approved Certificate of Zoning Compliance must be obtained prior to the installation of: any new patios, walkways, driveway expansions, parking spaces, storage sheds, electric/gas generators, utility structures, swimming pools or outdoor dining areas, as well as a home occupation. The CZC must also be obtained prior to any change in use of a property, as determined by the Planning Director. Approved Certificates are void if construction does not begin within one year from the approval date. No Zoning Certificate is required for structures 200-square-feet or less. 
**All businesses are required to have an approved zoning certificate regardless of size.
What to submit with the CZC application
In addition to completely filling out this application, please include a site plan showing existing and proposed site conditions. The site plan shall include dimensions and distances from property lines for all structures. Please also include any drawings or renderings of the proposed improvement(s). 
Garage, Shed, and Storage Structure regulations
Sheds and other storage structures must maintain a side and rear yard setback of at least six feet from the rear property line and three feet from side property lines, and must not occupy any part of a front yard or easement. Additionally, detached accessory structures must be a minimum of 10ft from the principal structure. Height is limited to fourteen feet. Accessory buildings shall not exceed 50% of the principal building floor area or 900 sq ft, whichever is less. 
Recreational Structure regulations - Exempt from provisions of zoning code except for height limitations
Swing sets, playground equipment, garden trellises, well-head covers, etc. accessory to a residential use are exempt from provisions of zoning code except for height limitations
Doll houses and Club houses or other similar structures are considered as sheds for all intents and purposes.
Patio Structure regulations
Patio structures (pergolas, trellises, outdoor bars, fireplaces, outdoor kitchens, etc.) must maintain a side and rear yard setback of at least six feet from the rear property line and 3 feet from the side property line, and must not occupy any part of a front yard or easement. Height is limited to 14 feet. 
Generator and other Mechanical Device regulations
Mechanical Devices (air conditioners, heaters, rain barrels, etc.) must maintain a side and rear yard setback of at least three feet from property lines, and must not occupy any part of a front yard or easement. Height is limited to 80 inches from grade. 
Pavilions and Other Open-Sided Structure regulations (detached from the main building)
Gazebos, Pergolas and other open-sides structures may not exceed 14 feet in height . The structure must be located in the rear yard buildable area.

record_types.text:
Application is hereby made for a DEVELOPMENT PERMIT as required by the City of Hilliard for development in an identified flood hazard area. All activities shall be completed in accordance with the requirements of said regulations. The development to be performed is described below and in attachments hereto. The applicant understands and agrees that:
• The permit applied for, if granted, is issued on the representations made herein;
• Any permit issued may be revoked because of any breach of representation;
• Once a permit is revoked all work shall cease until the permit is reissued or a new permit is issued;
• Any permit issued on this application will not grant any right or privilege to erect any structure or sue any premises
described for any purposes or in any manner prohibited by the ordinances, codes, or regulations of the municipality;
• The applicant hereby gives consent to the Floodplain Administrator to enter and inspect activity covered under the
provisions of the floodplain regulations;
• If issued, the FHA Development Permit form will be posted in a conspicuous place on the premises in plain view; and,
• If issued, the permit will expire if no work is commenced within one year of issuance.
In addition to completion of this form the applicant agrees to submit any additional information required by the floodplain administrator in order to determine that the proposed development is compliant with the local and federal flood damage prevention criteria of the National Flood Insurance Program. Site plans for all development proposals must:
• Be drawn to scale with north arrow.
• Show property boundaries, floodway, and floodplain lines.
• Show dimensions of the lot.
• Show dimensions and location of existing and/or proposed development on the site. 
• Show areas to be cut and filled.
Applications for residential and non-residential structures must also include:
• The proposed lowest floor elevation based on the datum used on the effective Flood Insurance Rate Map and base flood elevation for the site.
• Identification of whether the structure has a basement or enclosure below the lowest floor, and if it contains a basement or enclosure, detailed drawings showing foundation openings to allow passage of floodwaters.
• Description of how building utilities will be protected from flood waters including drawings showing locations of such utilities.
• Detailed description of anchoring system for all mobile and manufactured homes.
• Description of construction materials that will be used below the flood protection elevation.
An existing structure must comply with the flood protection standards if it is substantially improved (an improvement equal to or greater than 50% of the market value of the structure). The "substantial improvement" definition applies to existing structures only and that once a structure meets the definition of "new construction" any further improvements to that structure must meet "new construction" requirements. For floodplain management purposes "new construction" means structures for which "start of construction" began on or after the effective date of the initial Flood Insurance Rate Map issued by FEMA for the community.
Any Pre-FIRM structure within the SFHA that has sustained damage from any source (flood, fire, etc...) must be evaluated to determine if the structure is “substantially damaged” (damaged to 50% or more of the market value of the structure). If the structure is “substantially damaged, the structure must be brought into compliance with the flood protection standards.
For subdivision proposals greater than 5 acres or 50 lots, or large-scale developments greater than 5 acres, a hydrologic and hydraulic analysis must be conducted to determine base flood elevations in flood hazard areas where no base flood elevations are provided.
A Conditional Letter of Map Revision (CLOMR) must be obtained for proposed projects that would result in more than a 1.0 foot increase in BFE on a watercourse that has been studied through detailed hydrologic and hydraulic analyses where BFEs have been specified, but no floodway has been designated OR when a project proposed (totally or partially within the floodway) along a waterocurse for which detailed analyses have been conducted and BFEs and a floodway have been designated would result in any (greater than 0.0 foot) increase in the BFE.
Applications for non-residential structures proposed to be floodproofed must have a completed FEMA floodproofing certification form attached (can only be completed by a Registered Professional Engineer or Architect).

departments.name: Contractor Registration
departments.text:
Hilliard requires all contractors working in the city to be registered. Registration is for a calendar year and must be renewed annually. Registrations applied for in December will be good for the following year.
729.02 - REGISTRATION REQUIREMENTS.
(a)Within the corporation limits of Hilliard, no person shall act as or claim to be a heating-ventilating-air conditioning contractor, refrigeration contractor, plumbing contractor, electrical contractor, or hydronics contractor unless that person holds or has been assigned an Ohio Construction Industry Licensing Board (OCILB) specialty contractor's license pursuant to Chapter 4740 of the Ohio Revised Code (ORC) for the type of contractor that person is acting as or claiming to be. In addition, any person engaged in, or wanting to be engaged in, any of the specific contractor types listed above shall have a current, valid OCILB specialty contractor license and apply for, and be duly registered with the City of Hilliard, in order to apply for and obtain permits to perform work of their specific OCILB licensed craft or trade. No specialty contractors holding a valid OCILB license shall perform any work or services within the City unless they have first secured a Certificate of Registration as provided in subsection (c) below.
(b)No general contractor, demolition contractor, home improvement contractor, sewer line layer (builder or tapper), or any business or individual offering the aforementioned services, for a fee other than as an employee of a registered contractor with the City, shall perform any work within the City unless they have first secured a Certificate of Registration from the City as provided in subsection (c) below.
(c)Any person desiring to conduct, carry on or engage in any of the work or provide the services listed in subsection (a) or (b) above, shall make written application for registration on forms made available by the City's Building Department. Upon submission of a complete application and the required fee, and contingent upon meeting requirements of this Chapter, registrations shall be issued by the City Manager or his/her designee.

projects.text:
Hilliard’s Solar Energy Resources
Welcome to the City of Hilliard’s solar resources landing page. The Hilliard Community Development Department is committed to exceptional customer services, and this webpage constitutes a collection of solar information and resources to encourage solar energy development in our community.
The City of Hilliard is working to become a SolSmart designated community by implementing best practices to make it easier for residents and businesses to install and access solar energy. Information about our community's solar goals can be found in our Solar Statement (https://viewpointcloud.blob.core.windows.net/profile-pictures/PR-1_HilliardSolarStatement_Thu_Aug_04_2022_14:58:54_GMT+0000_(Greenwich_Mean_Time).pdf).
For more information about the basics of solar energy, your solar options, and important questions to consider, please read the Residential Consumer Guide to Solar Power (https://www.seia.org/research-resources/residential-consumer-guide-solar-power) and visit the Department of Energy’s Homeowner’s Guide to Going Solar (https://www.energy.gov/eere/solar/homeowners-guide-going-solar). You can also learn more about solar companies in Ohio by clicking here (https://www.seia.org/state-solar-policy/ohio-solar).
City of Hilliard Solar Policies & Processes
Our Solar Permitting Checklist (https://viewpointcloud.blob.core.windows.net/profile-pictures/Solar_Permit_Checklist__Wed_Aug_11_2021_15:43:39_GMT+0000_(Greenwich_Mean_Time).pdf) provides clear guidelines about the permitting and inspection processes for solar energy in Hilliard. Any property owner or registered contractor can apply for a solar energy system permit. A high-level overview and facts about zoning rules concerning solar panel installments are located at the top of page 1.
Solar Benefits
Solar energy uses a renewable energy source–the sun–and provides many benefits for individuals and the community. It improves environmental quality by reducing carbon emissions and air pollution, supports local solar companies, increases electric grid resilience during peak demand, and can even save money on energy costs as the prices continue to drop from technological developments.
Solar Maps & Potential
• Investigate your property’s solar potential by clicking here (https://www.google.com/get/sunroof#p=0). You can also estimate the performance of potential PV projects using the National Renewable Energy Laboratory’s PVWatts Calculator (https://pvwatts.nrel.gov/index.php). (https://sunroof.withgoogle.com/data-explorer/place/ChIJMxtWksaWOIgRnlXah9jo_aE/)
• Estimated Rooftop Solar Potential for Hilliard (https://sunroof.withgoogle.com/data-explorer/place/ChIJMxtWksaWOIgRnlXah9jo_aE/)
Finding a Solar Contractor
• NABCEP (http://www.nabcep.org/certified-installer-locator) Professional Directory –­ Find certified energy practitioners who can assess your home for solar energy.
• EnergySage (https://www.energysage.com/) – Learn about solar energy and get solar quotes from a network of pre-screened, local solar installers.
• Solar Owner’s Manual (https://solsmart.org/wp-content/uploads/English-SolarUnitedNeighbors-Solar-Owners-Manual-2021.pdf) – Information for current solar homeowners to ensure they are getting the most out of their system from Solar United Neighbors.
• Solar Customer Resource Portal (https://www.seia.org/initiatives/solar-customer-resource-portal) – Solar resources from the Solar Energy Industries Association (SEIA).
• Consumer Solar Checklist (https://irecusa.org/programs/consumer-protection/checklist/)– A checklist for residential consumers considering solar energy from the Interstate Renewable Energy Council (IREC).
• Clean Energy Consumer Bill of Rights (https://irecusa.org/programs/consumer-protection/bill-of-rights/) – Use this document to determine what you are entitled to as a solar consumer.
Financing, Incentives, and Tax Exemptions
• See what Federal (https://programs.dsireusa.org/system/program?state=US) and State (https://programs.dsireusa.org/system/program/oh/solar) incentives are available for solar installations.
• Homeowner’s Guide to the Federal Tax Credit for Solar Photovoltaics (https://www.energy.gov/eere/solar/homeowners-guide-federal-tax-credit-solar-photovoltaics) – Learn about federal tax credits, eligibility, and other common questions & answers from the U.S. Department of Energy.
• A Homeowner’s Guide to Solar Financing (https://www.cesa.org/assets/2015-Files/Homeowners-Guide-to-Solar-Financing.pdf) – Learn about different financing options from the Clean Energy States Alliance (CESA).
